name: ATMOS ENERGY CORP
moat_justification: Exclusive regulated gas-distribution franchises with captive, essential-service customers and rider mechanisms that put new capex into rates quickly, plus the APT intrastate pipeline/storage franchise in Texas — a durable, visible rate-base compounding machine ($26B FY2026–30 plan, rate base guided $18.8B to $40–44B). Capped at 6 because regulators set the allowed return (no pricing power beyond rate cases and riders), Texas political/regulatory scrutiny of riders and customer bills is rising, safety litigation is a live exposure, and the plan is funded with continuous debt plus equity issuance that grows the share count ~5.2%/yr, diluting rate-base growth per share.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 13 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
DILUTION: share count growing 5.2%/yr — already deducted via the growth adjustment; check SBC trend
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

SBC_TAG_RECONCILED: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense exceeds ShareBasedCompensation for FY2016 (14,760,000 vs 24,600,000, +66.7%), FY2017 (14,064,000 vs 23,100,000, +64.2%), FY2018 (12,863,000 vs 23,900,000, +85.8%), FY2019 (11,121,000 vs 23,900,000, +114.9%), FY2020 (9,583,000 vs 21,100,000, +120.2%), FY2021 (11,255,000 vs 24,100,000, +114.1%), FY2022 (10,743,000 vs 22,200,000, +106.6%), FY2023 (10,178,000 vs 23,700,000, +132.9%), FY2024 (10,709,000 vs 25,400,000, +137.2%), FY2025 (12,731,000 vs 33,200,000, +160.8%); the Allocated figure was used — the Share tag carries only part of stock compensation at this filer (a difference under 1% is tag rounding and needs one line in the analysis)
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Utilities sector — OE/capex DCF fits utilities names poorly; grade confidence low
one_liner: Durable Texas-heavy regulated gas monopoly, moat 6/10, but conservative owner's earnings are negative in 4 of the last 5 years (capex exceeds OCF on a $26B rate-base build; normalized base −$8.05/share after engine 5.5 adds the capitalized share of stock compensation) — Tier F on this screen; guided 6–8% EPS growth does not clear 15% and no hurdle-clearing price is computable on a negative OE base.
moat_for: Exclusive regulated gas distribution franchises — captive, essential-service customers, Texas-weighted
Rider/rate mechanisms recover safety and reliability capex quickly ($396M annualized operating-income increases implemented fiscal YTD 2026)
$26B FY2026–2030 capital plan; rate base guided from $18.8B to $40–44B by FY2030
APT intrastate pipeline/storage franchise riding Permian/Waha demand (APT spreads $4.66 vs $1.77 prior year, fiscal YTD 2026)
Steady customer growth — ~51,000 added in 12 months to June 30, 2026, ~39,000 in Texas
moat_against: Regulators cap returns — allowed ROE and rider recovery set politically; no pricing power beyond rate cases
Texas election-cycle scrutiny of riders and customer bills (Jefferies PT cut, Oct 1 2026) is the named key risk
Safety litigation/reputational exposure (Dallas Oak Cliff explosion wrongful-death suit)
Continuous debt + equity funding: share count +5.15%/yr dilutes per-share compounding
Long-run gas-distribution transition risk if electrification policy turns against residential gas
